_rule: The design's prose: architecture, operating model, rollout and risks. Numbers are not typed here — the page computes them from the kernel.

case.local: Nowhere: they stay on the company's laptops and core nodes.
case.corporate: To the vendor's cloud, under its terms and retention settings.

case.local: Only the company. No AI processor to contract, audit or monitor for inference.
case.corporate: The vendor, as processor — contracts, due diligence, sub-processors, yearly review.
Yes, if the model runs outside the UK/EEA: an adequacy route or safeguards, and a transfer risk assessment.

case.local: Owned capacity plus the people who run it. Volume growth costs hardware in steps.
case.corporate: Seats × people, plus tokens × volume. Growth costs in proportion.

case.aspect: Evidence of what the AI did
case.local: A signed, hash-linked receipt for every step, held by the company.
case.corporate: Vendor logs and dashboards, on the vendor's terms.

case.local: Open weights (Apache 2.0), hash-pinned; nobody changes it under you.
case.corporate: The vendor's model, updated on the vendor's schedule.

case.local: Open 32B-class models: good for drafting, extraction and routing; below frontier models on hard reasoning. Measured before every go-live.
case.corporate: Frontier models: the strongest general quality available.
Mostly the vendor's; integration and governance stay yours.

case.local: Nothing to leave: the data, the models and the receipts are already yours.

architecture.what: Staff laptops enrolled as AI nodes: Chrome or Edge running small open models on the laptop's own GPU (WebGPU). Triage, routing and screening. Enrolled by device policy, run only on mains power, disk-encrypted.
architecture.evidence: Measured in fallfloor: seconds per item, cold start, nothing lost when a node died.

architecture.what: A small rack of on-premises inference nodes running a 32B-class open model (Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct, Apache 2.0) for customer reply drafts, the staff knowledge assistant and KYC extraction. N + 1 for resilience.
architecture.evidence: Throughput is a planning figure until Phase 1 measures it on the chosen node.

architecture.what: Peer-to-peer WebRTC data channels inside the LAN; a desk dispatches work, keeps queues and reassigns work from a node that has gone. At-least-once delivery with de-duplication.
architecture.evidence: fallfloor: 0 of 100 items lost in both kill tests.

architecture.what: Every step is signed by the node that did it (Ed25519) and hash-linked to the step before; the ledger is replicated to two core nodes and kept for the retention period.
architecture.evidence: fallfloor: 898 hops, every signature re-verified in CI.

architecture.what: Deterministic gates on every output (the reply gate: right article, no invented numbers, links or emails) and a dual-map go/no-go gate on every deployment decision.
architecture.evidence: The board below, sealed from fallfloor's evidence.

architecture.what: A retrieval index over the bank's own documents (policies, help articles, procedures), built and stored on the core nodes.
The existing identity provider (single sign-on), role-based access to each AI system, a register of AI systems with a named owner each, and change control for model updates.
architecture.evidence: Design element; set up in Phase 0.

architecture.what: Connectors to the ticketing system, the email gateway and the HR system, running inside the network.
Agents approve customer replies; analysts confirm KYC records; the HR team answers the questions the router sends them.
architecture.evidence: The board decides where a person must stay in the loop.

architecture.what: Outbound traffic for AI is limited to fetching model weights (no personal data) into a hash-pinned internal mirror. Closed by default.

operating: A named owner for every AI system, in a register the DPO can read (Phase 0).
AI literacy for everyone who operates or relies on an AI system — the AI Act Article 4 duty — with role-specific training for agents, analysts and the platform team.
A DPIA per workload before it touches personal data; the local design removes the transfer and processor sections from them.
Quarterly re-gating: every deployment decision is re-run on fresh measured evidence; a BLOCK stops it, a PENDING names what must be measured.
Change control for models: a new model or prompt goes through the same pre-registered test before it replaces the old one.

rollout.do: AI system register with owners; lawful basis and DPIA screening per workload; AI Act role map (provider and deployer for in-house systems); AI literacy plan; Article 50 notice wording; pre-register the Phase 1 thresholds.
rollout.gate: The CTO signs the register, the thresholds and the budget for one core node.

rollout.phase: Phase 1 — Pilot on your own data
rollout.do: One core node and twenty enrolled laptops; the fallfloor method on the bank's own (pseudonymised) tickets, messages and documents; measure core-node throughput, agent catch rate and quality per workload.
rollout.gate: Every decision re-run on the pilot's evidence. PASS goes to Phase 2; PENDING names the measurement still missing; BLOCK stays out.

rollout.do: Workloads that passed go live with a person in the loop: HR routing, reply drafts for agents, KYC extraction with analyst confirmation. Knowledge index built. Core nodes bought to the measured capacity.
rollout.gate: Monthly quality sampling against the pre-registered thresholds; incidents and data-subject requests handled through the normal processes.

rollout.do: The staff knowledge assistant to all knowledge workers; the floor to its enrolled laptops; seat licences not renewed where the local assistant measured good enough.
rollout.gate: Seat renewals are a CTO decision on measured usage and quality, not a default.

rollout.do: Quarterly re-gating, model upgrades through change control, capacity added in steps. High-risk uses (such as credit decisions) only through the AI Act high-risk regime, which applies from 2 December 2027.
rollout.gate: Each quarter's board is sealed and kept with the audit record.

limits: A modelled company: the volumes, team sizes, compliance days and day rate are assumptions, labelled and changeable on this page.
The measured evidence comes from one laptop in fallfloor, on public datasets. The bank's own data will score differently — that is what Phase 1 measures.
Core-node throughput is a planning figure from the node's published memory bandwidth, not a measurement.
The corporate side prices the same work, not the same quality: frontier models would very likely answer more of it correctly.
Staff are the largest line on both sides and rest on assumptions about team size; the cost section shows how much of each total rests on estimates.
The compliance map quotes the law and says what each stack does to each duty. It is a map for the CTO and DPO; counsel signs off the final position.
